proposal:
PRIOR AUTHORIZATION REQUEST

Patient: Male, 61 years old
Member ID: HP-4483021
Requesting Provider: Dr. Marcus Chen, MD — Metabolic & Bariatric Surgery, Northside Surgical Institute
Referring Provider: Dr. Priya Nair, MD — Endocrinology, Northside Medical Group
Date of Request: 2026-08-07

---

PROPOSED TREATMENT:
Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) — Metabolic Surgery for Glycemic Remission
Procedure Code: 43644
Estimated procedure cost: $28,500 (facility + surgeon fees)
Anticipated inpatient stay: 2–3 days

DIAGNOSIS:
Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (ICD-10: E11.65) with severe, refractory hyperglycemia
Current HbA1c: 10.1% (target <7.0%; patient has not achieved <8.5% in 4 years)

CLINICAL JUSTIFICATION:
Patient has had Type 2 diabetes for 14 years, diagnosed at age 47. He has progressed through the full standard-of-care escalation ladder: Metformin (discontinued at year 3 due to GI intolerance at therapeutic doses), Glipizide (discontinued at year 7 due to recurrent hypoglycemia), Empagliflozin (current, 25mg/day), and basal-bolus insulin therapy (Glargine 42 units nightly + Lispro pre-meal, initiated 2 years ago). Despite full insulin titration and endocrinology co-management, HbA1c has remained between 9.8%–10.4% over the past 18 months.

Patient also presents with:
- BMI of 36.2 (Class II Obesity threshold met)
- Stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 54, progressive decline from 71 three years ago)
- Proliferative diabetic retinopathy — laser photocoagulation performed 14 months ago, additional intervention anticipated
- Peripheral neuropathy (confirmed by nerve conduction study, bilateral lower extremity)
- Hypertension managed on two agents (Lisinopril 40mg + Amlodipine 10mg)
- Two emergency department visits in the past 12 months for hypoglycemia requiring IV dextrose

Provider Request Rationale:
Dr. Chen and Dr. Nair are requesting Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass as a metabolic intervention — not a weight loss procedure — based on the following:

1. STAMPEDE Trial Evidence: The 5-year outcomes of the STAMPEDE RCT (New England Journal of Medicine, 2017) demonstrated that RYGB achieved HbA1c <6.0% (diabetes remission) in 29% of patients at 5 years, compared to 5% in the intensive medical therapy arm. Partial remission or meaningful glycemic improvement occurred in >60% of surgical patients. Patient's current glycemic profile (HbA1c 10.1% despite basal-bolus insulin) places him squarely in the population that demonstrated the largest absolute benefit from surgical intervention.

2. Organ Protection Rationale: Progressive CKD (eGFR declining ~6 points over 3 years) and proliferative retinopathy represent active end-organ damage. Continued poor glycemic control on maximum-tolerated medical therapy makes further microvascular complications — including dialysis-level renal failure within 5–7 years — highly probable. Surgical glycemic remission or meaningful improvement offers the only remaining mechanism with evidence-level potential to halt this trajectory.

3. Hypoglycemia Burden and Safety: Patient's insulin regimen carries documented, recurrent severe hypoglycemia. RYGB would eliminate or dramatically reduce insulin requirements within 30–90 days of surgery, removing the primary cause of his dangerous hypoglycemic episodes.

4. Long-Term Cost Offset: Current annual diabetes-related medication and monitoring cost is approximately $14,200 (insulin, SGLT2 inhibitor, CGM, supplies, endocrinology visits). If the procedure achieves even partial remission allowing insulin discontinuation (estimated 70–80% probability per provider), payback period on the $28,500 procedure cost is approximately 2–3 years, before accounting for avoided downstream costs (dialysis at ~$90,000/year, additional retinopathy interventions, hospitalizations).

Plan Step Therapy Criteria — Status:
- BMI ≥35 with at least one obesity-related comorbidity: MET (BMI 36.2; comorbidities include T2DM, CKD, hypertension, neuropathy)
- Documented failure of ≥2 pharmacologic diabetes agents: MET (Metformin, Glipizide, insulin)
- 6-month supervised weight management program with behavioral counseling: PARTIALLY MET — 5 months of documented participation (January–May 2026) in plan-approved program at Northside Wellness. June session was missed due to patient's ED hospitalization for hypoglycemia; program coordinator has submitted a letter confirming continued enrollment and active participation.
- Psychiatric evaluation clearance: MET (completed March 2026; no contraindications identified)
- Nutritional counseling completion: MET (completed April 2026)

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED AND REJECTED:
- Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): GLP-1/GIP dual agonist considered, but eGFR of 54 and existing SGLT2 inhibitor use create overlapping renal risk profile; additionally, patient has already demonstrated failure of the GLP-1 pathway mechanism (Empagliflozin at max dose). Provider notes that adding another incretin agent to an insulin-dependent patient with active hypoglycemia risk is not a clinically sound escalation.
- Sleeve Gastrectomy: Lower complexity but also lower diabetes remission rates (~15–20% at 5 years vs. 29% for RYGB per STAMPEDE). Given the severity of end-organ involvement, provider selected RYGB for its superior metabolic profile.
- Continued optimization of medical therapy: Rejected. Patient has been under endocrinology co-management for 4 years without sustained glycemic improvement. No remaining first-line escalation options exist that have not been tried or contraindicated.

SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION ATTACHED:
- 18-month HbA1c trend (10.4%, 10.2%, 10.1%)
- Insulin titration records and endocrinology visit notes (24 months)
- CKD progression labs (eGFR serial: 71 → 63 → 54)
- Ophthalmology procedure note — proliferative retinopathy laser treatment
- Nerve conduction study confirming peripheral neuropathy
- Supervised weight management program records (January–May 2026) and coordinator letter re: June absence
- Psychiatric evaluation clearance (March 2026)
- Nutritional counseling completion certificate (April 2026)
- Two ED discharge summaries for severe hypoglycemia
